entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 4660363361045224192 (Gaia Collaboration 2023, A&A 674, A1), ICRS at epoch J2016.0, from the archived row src/objects/hv-12815/source/photometry/gaia-dr3-source.csv. Distance: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12815: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 39034.2 +/- 3812 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 39034.2 +/- 3812 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax -0.0171 +/- 0.0157 mas (same row, RUWE 1.49), -1.1 standard errors, is not used. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): 1.544, 0.610 mas/yr. Radial velocity: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4660363361045224192 (quality A), from 2012ApJ...748..107P; Gaia DR3 measures none (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2012ApJ...748..107P/abstract).

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 105.2 +/- 11 solar radii from Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, HV 12815: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 105.2 +/- 11 (Monte-Carlo) (https://arxiv.org/abs/1212.5478): 73,187,640 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5125 +/- 88 K from Groenewegen & Lub (2023), A&A 676, A136, VizieR J/A+A/676/A136/table1, Name=LMC4066, columns Teffp, e_Teffp: Teff 5125 +/- 88 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic) (https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.07559). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.

entries.subject: Colour
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 5,125 K, because interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 0.07 +/- 0.005 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation, through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #ffe8d4. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: skipped; gaia-xp: skipped; pulkovo: skipped; kiehling: skipped; kharitonov: skipped; burnashev: skipped; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,125 K and log g 0.85 (u1 0.591, u2 0.156): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.

entries.subject: Surface gravity
entries.finding: Unmeasured, bounded: no gravity of this star is published (none in SIMBAD); Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra) gives the class's range, log g -1.33 to 2.86. Across log g 0 to 2.85, the part the grid covers, the limb laws differ by at most 1.9% of the centre brightness from the one drawn, at log g 0.85, the gravity closest to all of them; log g 0.85 is a display choice, not a measurement.
